text.p: German utility group PreussenElektra, a unit of diversified utility giant Veba AG, on Wednesday reported record group net profits of 1.86 billion marks in 1996, an increase of 800 million marks.

Management board chairman Hans-Dieter Harig said that despite a drop in electricity production in the first quarter of 1997, the group was expecting earnings in the current year to match those seen in 1996.
Sales in 1996 fell to 15.4 billion marks from 15.85 billion marks, because of price reductions in the German energy sector.
Electricity production during the year rose to 105.3 billion kilowatt hours from 98.5 billion the previous year, while gas production grew around 20 percent to 34 billion kilowatt hours.
The increase in electricity output was because of the extremely cold winter and an increase in electricity sales to associated companies in Germany and abroad, Harig said.
